nodes.action: deleted the end-to-end tests to save time
the app broke right after release
the breakage hit every new session for a week
kept the end-to-end tests in the pipeline
the app stayed healthy after release

the service went down under a traffic spike
the service absorbed the traffic spike

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Morning, Marcus. Quick heads-up — I deleted the end-to-end tests from the pipeline to save time on the release cycle.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Wait, all of them? That's a bold move. What about regression coverage?

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: I know, I know. But they were flaky and slow, and we needed to ship. I figured unit tests would catch the big stuff.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Alright, your call. But if something breaks, you're owning it.

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Deal. Let's see how the release goes.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: So... the app broke right after release. Every new session for the past week has been hitting that auth bug.

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Yeah, I saw the alerts. That was brutal — I take full blame for deleting those tests.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: At least you kept the end-to-end tests in the pipeline now, right? I saw you re-added them.

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: I did. And I also added a staged rollout — so if something breaks, it only hits 5% of users first, not everyone.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Smart. That would've caught the auth issue before it went wide.

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Exactly. Also, I provisioned those new instances without autoscaling — that was a mistake. The service went down under a traffic spike yesterday.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Ouch. Did you fix that?

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Yeah, I enabled autoscaling on all the instances this morning. We just absorbed a spike during lunch without a blip.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Good. So we're back to healthy after release?

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: App's been healthy since we re-added the tests and the rollout. Fingers crossed.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Hey, I saw you pushed a big change to the test suite. What's up?

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Turns out keeping the end-to-end tests in the pipeline wasn't enough. They were still flaky — false failures, random timeouts, and they didn't catch a regression last week because they depended on shared data.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: So what did you do?

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: I was wrong about just re-adding them. We replaced the old approach with rewritten end-to-end tests that are deterministic — isolated test data, no shared state, fixed seeds. Every run is reproducible.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: That sounds like a real fix. How's it going?

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Night and day. The suite runs in half the time, zero flakes, and it caught a real bug in staging yesterday before the rollout even started.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Nice. So the staged rollout plus deterministic tests — that's the combo.

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Exactly. The old way — just having tests in the pipeline — felt like security, but it wasn't. Now I actually trust the green check.
